  wave_1 |>
    transmute(
      p_id,
      wave = 1,
      resp = future_earthquake

  wave_2 |>
    transmute(
      p_id,
      wave = 2,
      resp = future_earthquake

  wave_3 |>
    transmute(
      p_id,
      wave = 3,
      resp = future_earthquake
    ),

    transmute(
      p_id,
      wave = 4,

    ),

    transmute(

      wave = 6,
      resp = future_earthquake

      wave = 7,
      resp = future_earthquake

    transmute(

  # The balanced sample: only respondents who answered in every wave,

STUDY_AREA:
# When you think about the next 25 years in Oklahoma, do you think the risk
# (frequency and severity) of these hazards will increase, decrease, or
# stay about the same? Earthquakes
#
# S3OK Public Survey, University of Oklahoma Institute for Public
# Policy Research and Analysis. Rebuilds this chart from the public
# wave files and nothing else: change over # waves 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8.
# One line per little river watershed group.

library(tidyverse)
library(srvyr)

# Read as character: a column that is empty for its first thousand rows
# is otherwise guessed logical, which turns every real value after it
# into NA.
wave_1 <- read_csv(
  "Public_Wave_1_Survey_Data.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
)
wave_2 <- read_csv(
  "Public_Wave_2_Survey_Data.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
)
wave_3 <- read_csv(
  "Public_Wave_3_Survey_Data.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
)
wave_4 <- read_csv(
  "Public_Wave_4_Survey_Data.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
)
wave_5 <- read_csv(
  "Public_Wave_5_Survey_Data.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
)
wave_6 <- read_csv(
  "Public_Wave_6_Survey_Data.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
)
wave_7 <- read_csv(
  "Public_Wave_7_Survey_Data.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
)
wave_8 <- read_csv(
  "Public_Wave_8_Survey_Data.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
)

d <- bind_rows(
  wave_1 |>
    transmute(
      p_id,
      wave = 1,
      STUDY_AREA = study_area,
      resp = future_earthquake
    ),
  wave_2 |>
    transmute(
      p_id,
      wave = 2,
      STUDY_AREA = study_area,
      resp = future_earthquake
    ),
  wave_3 |>
    transmute(
      p_id,
      wave = 3,
      STUDY_AREA = study_area,
      resp = future_earthquake
    ),
  wave_4 |>
    transmute(
      p_id,
      wave = 4,
      STUDY_AREA = study_area,
      resp = future_earthquake
    ),
  wave_5 |>
    transmute(
      p_id,
      wave = 5,
      STUDY_AREA = study_area,
      resp = future_earthquake
    ),
  wave_6 |>
    transmute(
      p_id,
      wave = 6,
      STUDY_AREA = study_area,
      resp = future_earthquake
    ),
  wave_7 |>
    transmute(
      p_id,
      wave = 7,
      STUDY_AREA = study_area,
      resp = future_earthquake
    ),
  wave_8 |>
    transmute(
      p_id,
      wave = 8,
      STUDY_AREA = study_area,
      resp = future_earthquake
    )
) |>
  filter(!is.na(resp)) |>
  # The balanced sample: only respondents who answered in every wave,
  # so a change is a change in answers, not in who took part.
  filter(n() == 8, .by = p_id) |>
  # A person's group can change between waves, so each keeps the group
  # they were in at the first of these waves.
  mutate(STUDY_AREA = STUDY_AREA[which.min(wave)], .by = p_id) |>
  filter(!is.na(STUDY_AREA)) |>
  # A group with fewer than 20 respondents is not drawn.
  filter(n_distinct(p_id) >= 20, .by = STUDY_AREA)

d <- d |>
  mutate(
    resp = factor(
      resp,
      levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"),
      labels = c("Significantly decrease", "Decrease", "Stay about the same",
                 "Increase", "Significantly increase")
    ),
    STUDY_AREA = factor(
      STUDY_AREA,
      levels = c("Inside Little River Watershed",
                 "Outside Little River Watershed")
    )
  )

# Each wave on its own. The design clusters on the panelist for the
# same reason the bar chart's does; within one wave each person
# answers once.
est <- d |>
  as_survey_design(ids = p_id) |>
  group_by(STUDY_AREA, wave) |>
  summarise(
    # The average answer as a position among the options, 1 for the
    # first.
    value = survey_mean(as.integer(resp), vartype = "ci"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(est, aes(x = wave, y = value, color = STUDY_AREA)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = value_low, ymax = value_upp), width = 0.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq_along(levels(d$resp)),
    labels = levels(d$resp),
    limits = c(1, nlevels(d$resp))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = str_wrap(paste(
      "When you think about the next 25 years in Oklahoma, do you",
      "think the risk (frequency and severity) of these hazards",
      "will increase, decrease, or stay about the same?",
      "Earthquakes"
    ), 70),
    x = "Survey wave",
    y = "Average answer",
    color = "Little River watershed"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
